tldr:
Don't let the author mark their own homework. A model reviewing its code **in the same session** shares the reasoning that produced the bug. Telling it to be critical, or giving it **extended thinking**, doesn't fix that. A **second, independent instance** given only the code does.

For big PRs:

- **Per-file passes** catch local issues.
- A separate **integration pass** catches cross-file data flow.
- One giant pass dilutes attention and contradicts itself.

A **verification pass with a confidence per finding** lets you auto-post the sure ones and route the rest to a person, once the confidence is **calibrated**. The docs describe the same draft → review → refine chain as separate calls.
mentalModel: Proof-reading your own essay, you read what you meant, not what you wrote — thinking harder doesn't help; a friend who never saw your notes spots the typo at once. For a 14-chapter book, check each chapter on its own, then read the whole plot once for continuity. And sort the friend's notes by how sure they are.
whatItIs:
The exam guide covers multi-instance and multi-pass review architectures (Guide §6 · TS 4.6, p.19). The docs describe the
self-correction chain (generate → review against criteria → refine) as separate API calls. D1.8 plans the per-file +
integration split.

**Sub-concepts — each with its picture to remember**

| # | Sub-concept | 🧭 Mental model | ⭐ Exam reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Self-review limits | Proof-reading your own essay: you read what you meant. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Knowledge 1 |
| 2 | Independent reviewer instance | A friend who never saw your notes. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Knowledge 2, Skill 1 |
| 3 | Extended thinking isn't a fresh pair of eyes | Re-reading harder doesn't un-know your intent. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Knowledge 2 |
| 4 | Per-file passes | Check each chapter on its own. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Knowledge 3, Skill 2 |
| 5 | Integration pass | Then read the whole plot once for continuity. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Skill 2 |
| 6 | Verification pass + confidence | Sort the friend's notes by how sure they are. | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Skill 3 |
| 7 | Self-correction chain as separate calls | Draft, review, refine — each step logged. | 📘 docs |

**Self-review vs independent review**

| # | Aspect | Self-review (same session) | Independent instance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Context | The generator's reasoning | Only the code (+ criteria) |
| 2 | Questions its own decisions | Rarely | Yes |
| 3 | Fixed by “be critical” or extended thinking? | No (guide) | — |
| 4 | Result here | 0 findings | The page=0 bug found |

**One pass vs multi-pass** (a 14-file PR)

| # | Plan | Local issues | Cross-file flow | Contradictions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One pass | 2 / 4 | Missed | Yes (file_03 both ways) |
| 2 | Per-file passes only | 4 / 4 | Missed | No |
| 3 | ⭐ Per-file + integration pass | 4 / 4 | Caught | No |

**Confidence: routing vs escalation** (don't mix them up)

| # | Use of self-reported confidence | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Routing review findings (auto-post vs human), once calibrated | ⭐ TS 4.6 · Skill 3; TS 5.5 |
| 2 | Deciding when to escalate a customer case to a human | ⭐ TS 5.2 — an unreliable proxy |
howItWorks:
1. **Generated code?** Review it with a **new instance** that gets only the code and the criteria, not the generator's
   session.
2. **Large PR?** Run a **per-file pass** for each file, then an **integration pass** given the per-file summaries to check
   data flow across files.
3. **Many findings?** Run a **verification pass** that attaches a confidence to each finding. Calibrate the threshold on
   labelled data, auto-post above it, and send the rest to a person.

grounding.text: Explicit prompt chaining is useful when you need to inspect intermediate outputs or enforce a pipeline; the most common pattern is self-correction: generate a draft → have Claude review it against criteria → refine, each step a separate API call you can log, evaluate or branch.

grounding.text: Self-review is limited: a model keeps its reasoning context from generation and is less likely to question its own decisions in the same session; an independent review instance without that context catches subtle issues more effectively than self-review instructions or extended thinking; split large reviews into per-file local passes plus cross-file integration passes to avoid attention dilution and contradictory findings.

Skills: a second, independent Claude instance reviews generated code without the generator's reasoning; per-file passes for local issues plus separate integration passes for cross-file data flow; verification passes where the model self-reports confidence per finding to enable calibrated review routing.
Per-file passes plus a separate cross-file integration pass avoid attention dilution.

Self-reported confidence is a routing signal here (TS 4.6 S3) and must be calibrated (TS 5.5); TS 5.2 warns that it's an unreliable proxy for deciding when to ESCALATE a customer case — different decisions.

examPoints.text: Self-review is limited: the model keeps its generation reasoning and is less likely to question its own decisions in the same session.
Independent review instances (no prior reasoning context) catch subtle issues better than self-review instructions or extended thinking.
Multi-pass review: per-file local passes plus cross-file integration passes avoid attention dilution and contradictory findings.
Use a second, independent Claude instance to review generated code without the generator's reasoning.
Split large multi-file reviews into focused per-file passes plus separate integration passes for cross-file data flow.
Run verification passes where the model reports confidence per finding, to enable calibrated review routing.

variants.label: ✅ ⭐ independent reviewer · per-file + integration passes · confidence-based routing
variants.code:
from utils.mpreview_lab import (CANDIDATES, FILES, SCENARIO, finish, generate, integration_review, per_file_review,
                                 review, route, verify)   # SIMULATED generator + reviewers

if SCENARIO in ("self_review", "extended_thinking"):
    code = generate("paginate the orders list")
    # a SECOND, independent instance reviews the code - without the generator's reasoning
    review(code, session="new")

elif SCENARIO in ("large_pr", "cross_file"):
    # focused per-file passes for local issues...
    local = [f for path in FILES for f in per_file_review(path)]
    # ...plus an integration pass for data flow across files
    integration_review(FILES, summaries=local)

else:  # calibrated_routing
    verified = verify(CANDIDATES, with_confidence=True)   # each finding carries the model's confidence
    route(verified, auto_post_at=0.8)                        # high confidence -> auto-comment; the rest -> a human

finish()
variants.observe: self_review / extended_thinking: a new instance given only the code finds “page(items, 0, size) returns an empty page”. large_pr: 14 per-file passes catch all 4 local issues, no contradictions. cross_file: the integration pass catches “file_04 renames total → amount; file_12 still reads total”. calibrated_routing: 3 high-confidence findings auto-posted, 3 low-confidence to a human, no false positive posted.
variants.why: Each check is done by a reviewer with the right context: none of the generator's reasoning, one file at a time, then the whole flow.

                                 review, route, verify)   # SIMULATED generator + reviewers

elif SCENARIO in ("large_pr", "cross_file"):

    # ...plus an integration pass for data flow across files

else:  # calibrated_routing
    verified = verify(CANDIDATES, with_confidence=True)   # each finding carries the model's confidence

questions.q: Claude Code generates a pagination feature, and in the same session the developer asks it to “review your code critically”. It reports no issues, yet QA finds that page 0 returns an empty page, the third such miss this month. The team proposes enabling extended thinking for the self-review. What is the most effective change?
opts: Enable extended thinking as proposed, so the self-review reasons far more deeply about its own code.
Review with a second, independent instance that sees only the code, not the generator's reasoning.
Ask the same session to review the code three times, and treat any issue found even once as real.
Add “be extremely critical of your own work” to the review request made in the same session.
questions.explain: A model reviewing its own output in the same session keeps the reasoning that produced the bug, so it is unlikely to question it. An independent instance without that context catches more. A and C deepen or repeat the same biased review. D is an instruction that doesn't remove the bias.

questions.q: A single review pass over a 30-file pull request misses issues in the middle files, and in one review it called the same file both “fine” and “missing validation”. A teammate proposes switching to a model with a larger context window. How should you evaluate this?
opts: Adopt it, since a larger window gives each of the 30 files more room and therefore more attention.
Adopt it, and sort the files by size so the largest ones come first in the review prompt.
Reject it: use per-file passes for local issues plus a separate integration pass for data flow.
Reject it, and instead ask the single pass to give equal attention to every one of the files.
questions.explain: The cause is attention dilution across many files, not space. Per-file passes give each file consistent depth, and an integration pass covers what crosses files. A and B misread the cause as a lack of space. D instructs the model to do something one pass can't reliably do.

questions.q: Per-file review passes now find every local bug in a PR. But file_04 renames total to amount while file_12 still reads total, and nothing flags it. This kind of break reached production twice last quarter. What is missing?
opts: A rule telling each per-file pass to look up every renamed field across the rest of the repository.
A larger per-file context that also includes the files each file imports and is imported by.
A linter step that bans renaming fields in any PR that touches more than one file at a time.
A separate integration pass that checks data flow across files, given the per-file results.
questions.explain: Per-file passes see one file at a time, so cross-file breaks need a dedicated integration pass. A asks each per-file pass to do the integration pass's job. B blurs the focus that makes per-file passes work. D bans a legitimate change.

questions.q: A CI reviewer posts every finding as a PR comment, about 25 per PR, and developers now ignore most of them. The team wants confident findings posted automatically and uncertain ones sent to a person. It already has 500 findings labelled valid or invalid. What enables this?
opts: A verification pass giving a confidence per finding, with a threshold calibrated on the labelled set.
Posting only the first ten findings on each PR, since those tend to be the most important ones overall.
Adding “only report findings you are confident about” to the reviewer's main review prompt.
Sending every finding to a person first, so that nothing uncertain is ever posted automatically.
questions.explain: A verification pass that attaches a confidence to each finding enables routing. Calibrating the threshold on labelled data is what makes the score trustworthy, because raw self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated. B cuts findings by position. C is a vague instruction. D gives up the automation.

questions.q: A team builds a documentation pipeline as three API calls: draft, then review against a checklist, then refine. A colleague says one call with “write it and then fix it” would be simpler and save about 4 seconds per document. Auditors must be shown how each document was checked. What does the prompting guidance say about the chained version?
opts: It is obsolete on current models, since a single call now corrects all of its own work just as well.
It is only worth keeping when each of the three calls uses a different model.
It is the self-correction pattern; separate calls let you log, inspect and evaluate each step.
It should be replaced by extended thinking, which records every check the model makes.
questions.explain: The docs describe draft, review and refine as separate calls, a self-correction chain, because each step can be logged, inspected and evaluated. That is exactly what the auditors need. A and D lose the inspectable steps. B invents a condition.

faq.q: Isn't a separate API call the same as an independent instance?
faq.a: What matters is the context. A new call that doesn't include the generator's reasoning is independent. A call that replays the whole generation conversation isn't. The docs' self-correction chain is separate calls you can log and evaluate.

faq.q: D1.5 says self-reported confidence is unreliable — why use it here?
faq.a: Different decisions. TS 5.2 rejects confidence as the trigger for escalating a customer case. TS 4.6 uses per-finding confidence from a verification pass to route review findings, and TS 5.5 says to calibrate it against labelled data first.

faq.q: How is this different from D1.8?
faq.a: D1.8 is about planning: choosing prompt chaining for predictable reviews. This page is about running the review: independent instances, per-file and integration passes, and routing by confidence.
